Networks estimated separately for each group

Source: R/groups.R
psychnet_group.Rd

A psychnet_group holds networks estimated separately for each group: one fitted network per level of the grouping variable, estimated with the same method and settings. When the same variables are measured in several groups, such as clinical and control samples, cohorts or occasions, these networks show how the association structure differs between them.

It is returned by psychnet() with group. print() lists the groups with their numbers of nodes and edges and their sample sizes, summary() returns these counts as a table, and as.data.frame() stacks the edges of all groups; cograph::splot() draws the networks in a grid. The analysis functions net_centralities(), net_predict(), net_boot(), net_stability(), net_casedrop_reliability() and net_split_reliability() accept the object and return one result per group (a psychnet_result_group); net_compare() tests the difference between two of its levels.

Resampling and comparison assume independent rows. Groups formed from several occasions per actor of an event log are refused by these functions, because they would need resampling at the actor level.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_group'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

A psychnet_group object.

...

Ignored.

row.names, optional

Ignored.

object

A psychnet_group object.

Value

print() returns x invisibly, after printing one row per group with its numbers of nodes and edges and its sample size.

as.data.frame() returns a data frame with one row per edge per group and columns group, from, to and weight.

summary() returns a data frame with one row per group (or per group and level when a group holds within-actor and between-actor networks) and columns group, nodes, edges and mean_abs_weight.

Details

Groups are ordered by the levels of the grouping variable when it is a factor, so its first level is group 1 in net_compare(), and otherwise by first appearance. Each network keeps the rows it was estimated from, so two members can be passed to net_compare() directly.

Conditions

psychnet_rows_dropped (warning) when rows with a missing group value are dropped; psychnet_bad_input when a group column is missing, a level is the empty string, there are fewer than 2 levels, or a level of a numeric table has fewer than 3 rows; psychnet_small_sample (warning) when a level has no more rows than variables.

See also

psychnet() to estimate the networks; psychnet for a single network; net_compare() to compare two groups.

Examples

d <- rbind(data.frame(SRL_GPT, source = "GPT"),
           data.frame(SRL_Claude, source = "Claude"))
nets <- psychnet(d, method = "glasso", group = "source")
nets
#> <psychnet_group> 2 networks by source (method: glasso)
#>   group nodes edges   n
#>     GPT     5    10 300
#>  Claude     5    10 300
summary(nets)
#>    group nodes edges mean_abs_weight
#> 1    GPT     5    10       0.2444301
#> 2 Claude     5    10       0.3536997
as.data.frame(nets)
#>     group from to       weight
